items.text: Since we know that life exists on Earth. <break time="0.8s" /> We are most likely to find it and recognize it. <break time="0.8s" /> On other worlds that resemble Earth. <break time="0.8s" /> This is the logic. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the search for Earth like planets in other systems. <break time="0.8s" /> And the terracentric search for life on those worlds. <break time="0.8s" /> It fuels the drive to follow the water. <break time="0.8s" /> It forms the basis for seeking planets. <break time="0.8s" /> Where liquid water and protective atmospheres exist. <break time="0.8s" /> Preferably on medium sized, rocky planets. <break time="0.8s" /> With stable near circular orbits. <break time="0.8s" /> With daily and seasonal cycles that are not too extreme. <break time="0.8s" /> It underlies the concept of the stellar habitable zone. <break time="0.8s" /> Which assumes that life is restricted to those planets. <break time="0.8s" /> At just the right distance from their central star. <break time="0.8s" /> For Earth like conditions to exist. <break time="0.8s" /> It fits perfectly. <break time="0.8s" /> With the search for life in our own image. <break time="0.8s" /> The alternative logic is one. <break time="0.8s" /> That starts from a different assumption ―. <break time="0.8s" /> That life on Earth is not representative necessarily. <break time="0.8s" /> Of life elsewhere. <break time="0.8s" /> And that therefore the conditions. <break time="0.8s" /> That led to and sustain life on Earth. <break time="0.8s" /> Need not be viewed as limitations. <break time="0.8s" /> A nuanced version of this alternative is. <break time="0.8s" /> That, in fact, the life we see around us as humans. <break time="0.8s" /> Is not even typical of the vast majority of biomass on Earth. <break time="0.8s" /> The unseen microbial world beneath our feet, in our oceans. <break time="0.8s" /> And to a considerable depth within the crust of our planet. <break time="0.8s" /> Is the rule for life on most worlds. <break time="0.8s" /> Including our own. <break time="0.8s" /> With the larger organisms that catch our eye. <break time="0.8s" /> Simply being the exceptions that command our attention.
